patient.name: Marcus Whitfield
patient.chiefComplaint: Fall with head injury, decreased level of consciousness

history.hpi: Coworkers report the patient fell approximately 12 feet from scaffolding at a construction site, striking his head on a concrete pad. He was initially moving and moaning immediately after the fall but has progressively become less responsive over the several minutes since. No other injuries are apparent; he was wearing a hard hat that came off on impact.
history.lastOralIntake: Lunch approximately 1 hour prior to the fall
history.events: Coworkers called 911 immediately after witnessing the fall; patient's mental status has declined since bystanders' initial assessment

scene.dispatch: 35-year-old male, fall from height, altered mental status, construction site
scene.location: Active construction site, patient supine on a concrete pad beneath scaffolding, hard hat lying nearby
scene.safety: Scene secured by site foreman; overhead scaffolding work halted; no ongoing hazards
scene.bystanders: Several coworkers present, one witnessed the fall and can describe the mechanism
visualCues: Patient supine on concrete, hard hat several feet away with a visible crack
Small scalp laceration with minimal bleeding
No other visible deformity or wounds
Scaffolding approximately 12 feet above the patient's position

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 35-year-old male supine on concrete, unresponsive to voice, with a small scalp laceration and no other visible trauma. Isolated severe head injury is suspected from the witnessed 12-foot fall.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but snoring respirations, occasional gurgling
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Irregular rate and depth, 22/min with brief pauses
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong, skin warm and dry
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil sluggish and slightly larger than right; right pupil reactive
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws from pain on right side; left side shows only extension posturing
otherFindings: Small scalp laceration with minimal oozing
No midline spinal tenderness elicited on palpation
No other visible deformity, chest/abdomen/pelvis/extremities unremarkable on exam
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Moans to painful stimuli only, no intelligible words

expectedActions.shortAction: High-flow oxygen via NRB; head of board elevated 30 degrees
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer high-flow oxygen via NRB (non-rebreather) as a precaution against unanticipated deterioration. Severe head injury – Elevate head of bed 30 degrees
expectedActions.rationale: Preoxygenation and head elevation reduce ICP and buy time before hypoxia during intubation attempts.

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain manual cervical stabilization throughout airway management
expectedActions.rationale: Moderate/severe head injury carries assumed concomitant cervical spine injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as contributing cause of AMS
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Evaluate for other causes of altered mental status — check blood glucose during transport
expectedActions.rationale: AMS following trauma may have a treatable metabolic contributor that must be excluded.

expectedActions.shortAction: Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive-pressure ventilation for at least 2 minutes before RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure.
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate preoxygenation prevents peri-intubation hypoxia, which is especially harmful to an already-injured brain.

transitions.condition: Crew maintains manual cervical stabilization, applies high-flow oxygen via NRB, elevates the head of the bed/board 30 degrees, and checks blood glucose while preparing for advanced airway management.
The crew proceeds directly to induction and paralysis without completing the required 2 minutes of preoxygenation, risking peri-intubation hypoxia in a patient with an already injured brain.

phases.name: Preoxygenation and C-spine maintained
phases.description: Crew maintains cervical stabilization, applies high-flow oxygen, elevates the head of the bed, and prepares equipment and medications for RSI given the patient's inability to protect his airway (GCS 6).
phases.triggerCondition: The primary survey confirms no airway obstruction, breathing, or massive hemorrhage requiring immediate intervention beyond oxygen; given GCS 6 with irregular respirations and loss of protective airway reflexes, the crew begins high-flow preoxygenation and RSI preparation per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent with NRB in place, occasional snoring
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong, skin warm and dry
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil sluggish and slightly larger than right; right pupil reactive
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws from pain on right side; left side shows only extension posturing
otherFindings: RSI equipment and medications prepared and checked

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 85 mcg IV premedication (85 kg × 1 mcg/kg), 2-3 min prior to intubation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider pre-medication with Fentanyl, 1 mcg/kg, 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt.
expectedActions.rationale: Blunts the sympathetic/hemodynamic response to laryngoscopy, which can otherwise spike ICP.

expectedActions.shortAction: Etomidate 25 mg IV push induction (85 kg × 0.3 mg/kg = 25.5 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Etomidate provides hemodynamically neutral induction, avoiding the BP swings that worsen cerebral perfusion in TBI.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 85 mg IV push paralytic (85 kg × 1 mg/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Provides paralysis for first-pass intubation success without the transient ICP-elevating fasciculations of succinylcholine.

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer NS/LR bolus proactively to maintain SBP ≥ 110 mmHg; do not wait for hypotension
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Adult (age greater than 10 years): maintain SBP greater than or equal to 110 mmHg. Administer normal saline (NS)/lactated Ringer's (LR) fluid boluses to maintain SBP above threshold. Do not wait until after the patient is already hypotensive—prevent hypotension
expectedActions.rationale: Cerebral perfusion pressure depends on maintaining adequate systemic BP; induction agents and positive-pressure ventilation both risk dropping preload.

transitions.condition: After a full 2 minutes of high-flow preoxygenation and positive-pressure ventilation, the crew proceeds with RSI per protocol using premedication, an induction agent, and a paralytic.

phases.name: Preoxygenated, RSI performed
phases.description: With adequate preoxygenation complete, the crew performs RSI using premedication, an induction sedative, and a paralytic, dosed by the patient's weight.
phases.triggerCondition: After 2 full minutes of high-flow preoxygenation with maintained SpO2 ≥97%, the crew proceeds with drug-assisted airway management given the patient's GCS 6 and loss of protective airway reflexes.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Being actively managed, BVM/NRB in place pre-attempt
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Assisted, adequate chest rise with BVM
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil sluggish and slightly larger than right; right pupil reactive
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sedated and paralyzed, no spontaneous movement
otherFindings: Two experienced airway practitioners present at bedside
Continuous waveform capnography attached and ready

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm tube placement with waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds, absent gastric sounds
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds.
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation method and must be documented immediately after placement.

expectedActions.shortAction: Ventilate to EtCO2 35-45 mmHg (target 40); avoid hyperventilation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Do not hyperventilate patients: Maintain all patients in EtCO2 range of 35–45 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperventilation causes cerebral vasoconstriction and worsens secondary brain injury absent herniation signs.

transitions.condition: Intubation succeeds on first pass within 15 seconds; waveform capnography confirms placement, and ventilation is titrated to an EtCO2 target of 40 mmHg while SBP is maintained above 110 mmHg.

phases.name: Tube confirmed, EtCO2 targeted
phases.description: The tube is confirmed and secured, ventilation is titrated to a normal EtCO2 target, SBP is maintained above threshold, and the patient is transported to the highest level of trauma care.
phases.triggerCondition: Following successful RSI and intubation, the crew confirms and secures the tube, sets ventilation to avoid both hypo- and hyperventilation, and prepares for transport.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured with endotracheal tube, confirmed placement
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mechanically/manually ventilated, equal bilateral breath sounds
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil sluggish and slightly larger than right; right pupil reactive, unchanged
otherFindings: ETT secured at appropriate depth, confirmed with continuous waveform capnography
No gastric sounds on auscultation over epigastrium
Cervical collar applied to help stabilize tube position

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to highest level of trauma care available
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Preferential transport to highest level of care within trauma system: GCS 3–13, P (pain) or U (unresponsive) on AVPU scale
expectedActions.rationale: GCS 6/AVPU-P meets criteria for preferential transport to the highest level trauma center.

transitions.condition: During transport, the left pupil becomes fixed and dilated and the patient develops decerebrate posturing — signs of herniation requiring brief modest hyperventilation per protocol.

phases.name: RSI without adequate pre-oxygenation
phases.description: The crew pushes induction and paralytic agents without completing the required preoxygenation period. SpO2 falls during the attempt, and the Cushing response becomes more pronounced as hypoxia compounds the rising intracranial pressure.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew proceeds directly to RSI without at least two minutes of high-flow preoxygenation and positive-pressure ventilation; SpO2 drops during the attempt and bradycardia with a widened pulse pressure emerges.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Apneic during attempt, no assisted ventilation in progress
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil now fixed and dilated; right pupil sluggish
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sedated and paralyzed, no spontaneous movement
otherFindings: No preoxygenation period was completed before drugs were pushed

expectedActions.shortAction: Abort attempt, resume BVM with high-flow O2 and PEEP, re-preoxygenate before re-attempting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attempt intubation, limiting attempts to 15 seconds, or a desaturation below 90%, whichever occurs first. Significant attention should be paid to avoiding hypoxia and hypotension during intubation attempts to limit patient morbidity and mortality.
expectedActions.rationale: Peri-intubation hypoxia compounds secondary brain injury on top of the primary TBI; the attempt must be aborted and the patient re-oxygenated before any further attempt.

phases.name: Herniation signs develop en route
phases.description: En route, the left pupil becomes fixed and dilated and the patient develops decerebrate posturing, signaling herniation. Per protocol, brief modest hyperventilation is permitted while other measures are optimized.
phases.triggerCondition: During transport, the crew reassesses and finds a newly fixed, dilated left pupil with decerebrate posturing — signs of herniation warranting a brief period of modest hyperventilation per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil fixed and dilated (new); right pupil sluggish
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Decerebrate posturing noted (extension of all extremities)
otherFindings: New finding on reassessment during transport
Widening pulse pressure and further bradycardia noted

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize herniation signs: new unilateral fixed/dilated pupil and decerebrate posturing
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: In patients with severe head injury with signs of herniation (unilateral dilated pupil or decerebrate posturing), modest hyperventilation to EtCO2 no less than 30 mmHg may be considered for a brief time
expectedActions.rationale: These are the specific protocol-defined triggers for the herniation exception to the standard EtCO2 target.

expectedActions.shortAction: Adjust ventilation to brief modest hyperventilation, EtCO2 target no lower than 30 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: to appropriately but not excessively hyperventilate patients with signs of herniation only to maintain EtCO2 30–35 (no lower than 30)
expectedActions.rationale: Only in the presence of true herniation signs is brief hyperventilation appropriate, and it must not drop EtCO2 below 30.
